paper_metadata.title: Achieving remarkable enhancement of yield strength and high ductility in a fine-grained Mg-6Zn-0.2Ca alloy via rotated hard-plate rolling

evidence.quote: a novel Mg-6Zn-0.2Ca alloy prepared via rotated hard-plate rolling (RHPR) exhibits a simultaneous high yield strength (YS) of ~268 MPa and ductility of ~22%
Mg-6.3Zn-0.24Ca ( wt. % ) (ZX602) extruded plates with ~40 mm in width and ~5 mm in thickness were used as initial materials in the study.

A multi-stage homogenization with three isothermal stages (320 ◦C for 2 h, 400 ◦C for 2 h and 450 ◦C for 5 h) followed by water quenching was carried out in a resistance furnace.

parameters.deformation: total thickness reduction ~80% over four passes; pass reductions ~50%, ~40%, ~30%, ~15%

evidence.quote: The sample wrapped with hard plates was pre-heated at 275 ◦C for 12 min and at 250 ◦C for 10 min before the first two passes and following two passes, respectively. The constant roller temperature was set as 100 ◦C.
Finally, both CR and RHPR samples were annealed at 250 ◦C for 5 min to relieve residual stress.

parameters.deformation: total thickness reduction ~80% over four passes along same direction to ~1 mm; pass reductions ~50%, ~40%, ~30%, ~15%

evidence.quote: the samples were continuously rolled at 300 ◦C to a final thickness of ~1 mm via four passes along the same rolling direction, with the thickness reduction of ~50%, ~40%, ~30% and ~15% from the 1st to the 4th pass
Finally, both CR and RHPR samples were annealed at 250 ◦C for 5 min to relieve residual stress.
Combined with XRD pattern ( Fig. 3 d), these particles are identified as Ca2Mg6Zn3 phase, which is the dominant phase in Mg-Zn-Ca alloys when the ratio of Zn/Ca is higher than 1.23
suggesting a fully coherent interface between α-Mg and spherical and needle-like MgZn2 phase

attributes.size: spherical ~80 nm; needle-like average length ~2 um, width ~0.3 um

evidence.quote: the CR sample contains fine spherical particles (~80 nm) and needle-like particles orient towards RD with an average length of ~2 μm and width of ~0.3 μm.

the RHPR sample displays more uniformly distributed fine spherical particles (~270 nm) without needle-like phase. The area fraction of spherical particles in the RHPR sample is significantly higher than that in the CR sample, i.e., ~7.7% vs. ~0.5%.
Both CR and RHPR samples possess a homogeneous fine grain structure with a similar grain size of ~4.1 μm and ~4.2 μm ( Fig. 4 c), respectively.

attributes.morphology: basal pole inclined ~14 deg towards RD, broad distribution 0-58 deg towards TD

evidence.quote: an ellipse-shaped texture, featuring an inclination of basal pole (~14◦) towards RD and a broad distribution (0-58◦) towards TD, is introduced in the RHPR sample. The peak intensity of the RHPR sample (~23.4) is significantly higher than that of CR counterpart (~12.0).
Both samples exhibit a relatively homogeneous fine grain structure (~4 μm) and a RD-split basal texture.

attributes.size: LAGB length per unit area ~3.04 um/um2

evidence.quote: the RHPR sample is saturated with abundant well-established LAGBs within grains, whereas the alloys processed by CR contain a limited fraction of LAGBs, i.e., ~49.1% vs. ~8.9%
